standards.name: EDAM (Ontology of data analysis and management)
standards.abstract: EDAM is an ontology of data analysis and data management (originally focused on bioinformatics but applicable beyond life sciences). It organises concepts that describe Topics (domains), Operations (functions/tools), Data types (and Identifiers), and Formats — i.e. descriptive labels for tools, workflows, datasets and related digital research objects. The resource is published and maintained by the EDAM community (developers, editors and contributors working with ELIXIR / IFB and other partners) and distributed as an OWL ontology with browsers and tooling. EDAM addresses the need for a consistent, machine-readable controlled vocabulary to annotate, find, compare and record provenance of computational resources (tools, workflows, data formats, training materials), and includes governance, contribution and technical processes (GitHub-based development, CI validation, and community extension projects such as EDAM Bioimaging).

classification.rationale: The source material is an ontology presented as hierarchical concept graphs with explicit relation types (a directed acyclic graph). The site also contains a short prose list of founding principles; therefore the standard legitimately includes a DAG structure plus a principles section.

principles.evidence:
"Principles

EDAM strives to uphold a few founding principles including:
Quality - an ontology that is moderated
Openness - development by the open community
Relevance - prioritising use-case-driven development towards comprehensive but practical coverage
Practicality - practical utility is valued over ontological “strictness” or any metaphysical doctrine
Clear scope - respecting the scope of other complementary, well-developed ontologies and open linked data efforts
Familiarity - including only concepts that are well established; familiar are prevalent and jargon is discouraged
Usability - conceptual hierarchy with sufficient richness but only necessary complexity
Maintainability - development must be efficient and sustainably up to date in the long term
EDAM is working towards implementing these principles fully and is open to suggestions."

topic.name: Topic
topic.description: A category denoting a rather broad domain or field of interest, of study, application, work, data, or technology.
topic.evidence: "Topic - A category denoting a rather broad domain or field of interest, of study, application, work, data, or technology."

operation.name: Operation
operation.description: A function that processes a set of inputs and results in a set of outputs, or associates arguments (inputs) with values (outputs).
operation.evidence: "Operation - A function that processes a set of inputs and results in a set of outputs, or associates arguments (inputs) with values (outputs)."

data.name: Data
data.description: Information, represented in an information artefact (data record) that is 'understandable' by dedicated computational tools that can use the data as input or produce it as output.
data.evidence: "Data - Information, represented in an information artefact (data record) that is 9understandable by dedicated computational tools that can use the data as input or produce it as output."

identifier.name: Identifier
identifier.description: A label that identifies (typically uniquely) something such as data, a resource or a biological entity.
identifier.evidence: "Identifier - \"A label that identifies (typically uniquely) something such as data, a resource or a biological entity.\""

format.name: Format
format.description: A defined way or layout of representing and structuring data in a computer file, blob, string, message, or elsewhere.
format.evidence: "Format - A defined way or layout of representing and structuring data in a computer file, blob, string, message, or elsewhere."

relations.name: Relation types
relations.description: EDAM defines a small set of relation types used to connect concepts, e.g. is_a, has_input, has_output, has_topic, is_identifier_of, is_format_of.
relations.evidence:
"Relation types

is_a

Defines a concept as a specialisation of another concept. ...

has_input

Defines an Operation concept as reading (inputting) a Data concept.

has_output

Defines an Operation concept as writing (outputting) a Data concept.

has_topic

Defines a Data or Operation concept as being within the scope of a Topic concept.

is_identifier_of

Defines that an Identifier concept identifies a Data concept.

is_format_of

Defines that a Format concept is the format of a Data concept."

standards.notes: Nodes and edges above capture the principal sub-ontologies and relation types described in the EDAM documentation (Topic, Operation, Data, Identifier, Format) and the principal relations (has_input, has_output, has_topic, is_identifier_of, is_format_of). Source pages: EDAM documentation (What is EDAM?, Technical details, Users Guide) and project materials (posters). OWL download: http://edamontology.org/EDAM.owl
